nodes.label: AgingBench: Longitudinal Agent Reliability Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Longitudinal benchmark for agent lifespan engineering measuring time-dependent reliability degradation in deployed agents across four aging mechanisms (compression, interference, revision, maintenance).

nodes.label: Agent Aging Taxonomy
nodes.rationale: Four mechanisms: compression aging (write-before-query barrier), interference aging (similar entries crowd out target fact), revision aging (changed state not updated correctly), maintenance aging (lifecycle events trigger regressions).

nodes.label: Temporal Dependency DAG
nodes.rationale: DAG structure encoding cross-session dependencies: version chains (fact supersession), dependency edges (probes requiring multi-session synthesis), interference pairs (confusable entities), accumulators (derived state).

nodes.label: Programmatic Task Generation
nodes.rationale: Seeded generators producing task streams at arbitrary scale with controlled pressure dials (dependency density, update rate, chain depth, interference count) enabling reproducible, mechanism-faithful evaluation.

nodes.label: Session Loop Evaluation
nodes.rationale: Formalized evaluation over N sessions where agent reads compressed memory, answers tasks and probes, receives score, and history is compressed for next session; lifecycle events injected at designated sessions.

nodes.label: Aging Curve Statistics
nodes.rationale: Half-life (sessions until 50% capability loss), decay slope (OLS fit), hazard proxy (per-session failure probability), final score, time-averaged score computed from aging curves.

nodes.label: Memory Pipeline Decomposition
nodes.rationale: Cyclic dataflow decomposed into Write (W), Read (R), Utilization (U), and Store (S) components; compression aging at W, interference at R, revision at U, maintenance at S.

nodes.label: Counterfactual Diagnostic Probes
nodes.rationale: Three probes (P1: baseline, P2: oracle retrieval, P3: oracle context) forming ablation ladder; differences yield utilization error, write error, and read error diagnostic profiles.

nodes.label: Seven Evaluation Scenarios
nodes.rationale: S1 (Research Literature), S2 (Lifestyle Assistant), S3 (Knowledge Base), S4 (Software Engineering), S5 (Self-Management), S6 (Naturalistic), S7 (Self-Planning) covering different deployment archetypes and mechanism combinations.

nodes.label: Tier-1 and Tier-2 Evaluation Tiers
nodes.rationale: Tier 1: runner-controlled ReAct agents with fixed memory policy enabling per-stage probes; Tier 2: autonomous CLI agents (OpenHands, Claude Code) with self-managed workspace memory.

nodes.label: 14 Models Across 7 Families
nodes.rationale: Open-source (Llama-3.1-8B, Qwen3-8B/14B, DeepSeek-R1-7B/14B, Gemma-4-31B, gpt-oss-120B) and closed-source (GPT-4o/4o-mini/5-mini, Claude Haiku/Sonnet/Opus) spanning 7B–120B.

nodes.label: Finding I: Aging is Multi-Dimensional
nodes.rationale: No single model dominates across mechanisms; rank reversals recur throughout Table 3; deployment-time model selection depends on which failure mechanism is most relevant.

nodes.label: Finding II: Behavioral and Factual Accuracy Decouple
nodes.rationale: On S2, constraint violations remain near zero while precision drops; aging is difficult to detect with behavioral metrics alone; requires mechanism-level probes testing fact recall.

nodes.label: Finding III: Revision Aging is Representational
nodes.rationale: Accumulator error shows no consistent improvement with larger models or better compression; failure stems from representation and update, not capacity; requires explicit state maintenance.

nodes.label: Finding IV: Write–Read Gap Persists
nodes.rationale: Across Tier 2, workspace fidelity exceeds downstream recall; agents retrieve too little information before answer generation; failure is utilization-stage, not write-stage.

nodes.label: Finding V: Within-Family Aging Asymmetries
nodes.rationale: Opus-4.7 has lowest pytest and ws_fid but competitive retrieval metrics; per-mechanism decomposition reveals write-time fidelity regression; same surface failure requires different repairs.

nodes.label: Typed-State Overlay Intervention
nodes.rationale: JSON sidecar maintaining numeric state alongside text memory; reduces accumulator error by 25% (lossy) to 47% (careful) at ~10% wall-time overhead; addresses revision-aging representational gap.

nodes.label: Threshold-Triggered Runtime Controller
nodes.rationale: Monitors per-session signals and fires corrective actions (typed-state overlay, compaction-prompt swap) when thresholds crossed; aggressive forward-only variant captures 91% of always-on ceiling at 86% wall time.

nodes.label: S8: SWE-Bench-Aging Scenario
nodes.rationale: Long-running developer agent on real OSS repository; eight curated GitHub issues from SWE-bench-Verified touching single Django ORM module; exercises all four mechanisms within longitudinal codebase.

nodes.label: Your Agents Are Aging Too (Zhu et al., 2026)
nodes.author: Zhu, Jianing et al.

nodes.label: TierMem: Tiered Memory for Agents (Zhu et al., 2026)
nodes.author: Zhu, Qiming et al.
nodes.rationale: Provenance-aware tiered memory distinguishing summary-caused omissions from reasoning failures; partial attribution predecessor to AgingBench's counterfactual framework.

nodes.label: MemoryArena: Benchmarking Agent Memory (He et al., 2026)
nodes.author: He, Zexue et al.
nodes.rationale: Multi-session memory benchmark with interdependent tasks; partial cross-session dependency support; AgingBench extends with full temporal DAG and lifecycle events.

nodes.label: LongMemEval: Long-Term Conversational Memory (Wu et al., 2024)
nodes.author: Wu, Di et al.
nodes.rationale: Benchmarks chat assistants on long-term interactive memory; single Q&A snapshot evaluation; AgingBench extends with longitudinal aging curves and mechanism-level diagnosis.

nodes.label: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting (Yao et al., 2022)
nodes.author: Yao, Shunyu et al.
nodes.rationale: Foundational agent loop combining reasoning and tool use; used as Tier-1 runner-controlled agent framework in AgingBench evaluation.

nodes.label: OpenHands: Open Platform for AI Software Developers (Wang et al., 2025)
nodes.author: Wang, Xingyao et al.
nodes.rationale: Open-source customizable agent framework supporting self-planning; used as Tier-2 autonomous agent in AgingBench evaluation.

nodes.label: Claude Code (Anthropic, 2026)
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: Production-level agent framework with CLI interface; used as Tier-2 autonomous agent in AgingBench evaluation.
